grades.rationale: Kyra is a cleric whose actual Fire domain focus spell, Fire Ray, attacks with a blazing band and deals fire damage; her source also describes Sarenrae’s fire-centered doctrine. This is a creature with an intrinsic fire ability, not merely an incidental item mention.

Burning Building is itself a hazard with the fire trait, and its Conflagration action damages occupants with fire while Spread propagates the burning condition to another building; this directly fits the broad fire discovery intent.

This young Fortune Dragon actor contains a real Fireball spell item, heightened to 5th rank and owned by its Arcane Spontaneous Spells entry with one 5th-rank slot. That is useful evidence of a creature carrying the spell, while the actor record is not the canonical spell document.

Firestarter Pellets are a consumable catalyst whose description says they modify a Fireball spell; the record is useful adjacent equipment context, but it is neither the spell nor a creature that owns it.

Greater Fireball Rune is a hazard whose Fireball action explicitly casts a 4th-rank Fireball spell for fire damage. This is a useful source for a Fireball effect, but the hazard record is not the canonical named spell document.

Koto Zekora’s actor owns two Fireball spell items, at 3rd and 5th rank, both associated with its Spontaneous Arcane Spells entry and the corresponding slots. The copied spells make this useful under an unfiltered query, though the actor is not the canonical spell document.

Tupilaq owns a Fireball spell item associated with Primal Innate Spells; its record gives a 3rd-rank spell heightened to 3rd with three innate uses. Under the explicit creature filter, the owner is an intentional useful match, even though this is not the canonical spell record.

Emriss’s actor contains a 3rd-rank Fireball spell associated with Divine Spontaneous Spells and a 3rd-rank slot. This directly identifies a creature that owns the spell for the filtered query, while remaining an actor record.

Asper Hajeri’s actor contains a 3rd-rank Fireball spell associated with Primal Spontaneous Spells and a 3rd-rank slot. This is useful under the creature filter because the actor owns the requested spell, though it is not the canonical spell document.

Arrogant Entodemonologist has a Fireball item tied to its Arcane Prepared Spells entry, and that entry’s 3rd-rank prepared slot contains the spell item ID. This is a direct filtered creature owner, not the canonical spell record.

The adult Fortune Dragon owns Fireball through Arcane Spontaneous Spells; this actor’s copy is heightened to 7th rank and associated with its 7th-rank slots. It is useful for a creature-filtered search but is not the canonical spell document.

This second Fortune Dragon (Young) actor record also owns the 3rd-rank Fireball item, heightened to 5th through its Arcane Spontaneous Spells entry. It is useful owner evidence, while the duplicate actor source is not the canonical spell document.

Barralbus’s complete actor item list contains an Arcane Prepared Spells entry and fire spells such as Produce Flame and Flaming Sphere, but no Fireball spell item or Fireball prepared slot. Fire-themed magic alone does not answer the exact Fireball query.

Lightlock is a magical room trap whose F8 trigger fires chilling dark fog at a creature carrying light; the action deals 10d6 cold damage and is explicitly named [quotation omitted] It directly fits a room-wide cold hazard, although it does not literally freeze victims.

Boreal Rage Trap operates in a room: it triggers when a creature enters marked areas or remains there for one minute, then breathes cold over a 15-foot burst; a critical failure causes frostbite. This directly fits a room hazard with cold/freeze effects.

Flooding Room is an enclosed mechanical trap that seals the room and eventually fills it with river water, but its full description gives falling-water bludgeoning damage rather than any cold or freezing effect. The room-hazard facet matches while the key effect is missing.
Familiar of Freezing Rime describes a familiar whose cold breath creates ice and difficult terrain, but it is a familiar rule rather than an enclosed room hazard and does not freeze room occupants.
Dead Faine is a living human with an occult spell that can mimic undead, but its source shows ordinary padded armor and no ghost, possession, or curse associated with that armor.

Lightweight Animated Armor is itself armor animated as a mindless construct through rituals or strange magic; it is a useful supernatural animated-armor alternative, but its source does not identify a haunting, possessing spirit, or curse.
Hansin is a living human gang leader carrying ordinary studded leather armor; the source provides no haunting, possession, or curse attached to either the creature or its armor.

Accursed Forge-Spurned is an undead dwarf in ordinary Full Plate, and its cursed item is a soul chain rather than the armor. That is related undead-and-armor context but does not provide haunted or cursed armor.

Animated Armor (BB) is a mindless construct whose source says suits of armor are animated by rituals or strange magic; it is a useful animated-armor supernatural alternative, though not specifically haunted, possessed, or cursed.

Graveknight’s Curse applies to anyone who wears a graveknight’s armor for at least an hour, prevents removal, and ultimately kills and transforms the wearer into the armor’s graveknight. This directly describes a cursed armor relationship.

Singing Shortbow is a real composite shortbow whose Song of Soothing restores 5d10 Hit Points to nearby creatures; it supplies both the bow and a healing effect, but the equipment record does not identify a creature owner who uses it.
Heal Companion restores Hit Points to an animal companion, so it is the healing half of the query, but this standalone spell record names no creature owner or bow use.
Feiya can heal others with her Occult Prepared Soothe spell and also carries a Crossbow; both capabilities belong to her character, but her listed weapon is a crossbow rather than a bow.
Staff of Healing (Major) has Heal among the spells it can cast, but it is only a staff item record and does not identify a creature owner or any bow.
Tsimaan has Medicine skill and expanded healer’s tools to perform healing checks, and owns a Crossbow; the same creature has healing and a similar ranged weapon, but the weapon is not a bow.
Dewey Daystar has an innate Heal spell and a Wand of Heal, so the actor can restore other creatures’ Hit Points; its complete inventory contains no bow, leaving the second requested capability unmet.

Lantern Archon owns a Heal spell associated with Divine Innate Spells, which can restore Hit Points to a willing living target; the creature record contains no bow, so it supplies only the healer side.

Stone-Breasted Owl has a primal innate Heal spell with two uses, and its Empowered Healing action increases the spell’s healing die; its inventory has no bow, so it does not meet the combined request.

Shalelu Andosana’s Soothing Mist is a healing focus spell that restores 2d8 Hit Points to a living target, associated with her Ranger Warden spellcasting entry and backed by three current focus points. The same actor carries Hunter’s Anthem, a longbow, and arrows, so the source shows both requested capabilities on her; its item state says worn with no hands held, so current wielding is not established.

Devise a Stratagem is an investigator action that assesses a foe and substitutes a previously rolled d20 for a Strike or skill check; its source contains no Attack of Opportunity name, old-name note, or reaction attack. It is a different action, so it does not answer the renamed-action lookup.

Venomfist is a water elemental whose own presence changes the weather over two miles to heavy rainfall, and its hostility turns nearby rain into a damaging toxic downpour. Its innate spell list also includes Wrathful Storm, an actual storm cloud with rain and gales. These are owned, active storm manifestations rather than incidental lightning vocabulary.

Diskah Night Watcher is a humanoid druid, not a storm being, but she owns usable storm-casting: Howling Blizzard is prepared in her 5th-rank Primal slot, and Tempest Surge is a Druidic Order focus spell with two focus points available. This is a useful storm-capable owner, while the record does not portray her as an embodied storm.
Living Boulder is an earth elemental that rolls across the Plane of Earth and glides through rock; its own description and abilities contain no storm, wind, rain, or lightning embodiment.

Living Graffiti (Chalk) is a construct painting that moves across flat surfaces and attacks with chalk; the source includes no storm manifestation or weather power. Its incidental Fireball reference only describes a way to destroy the surface it inhabits.
Storm Born is a druid feat that protects its bearer from penalties caused by weather and concealment in fog; it grants weather resilience, not a storm identity or a power to manifest storms.

Rite of Repatriation explicitly repairs damage to a culturally important object and can restore up to 5 Hit Points per ritual rank, potentially clearing broken. Its use is sharply limited: only damage since the rightful owners last possessed it qualifies, spirits must accept, it cannot replace missing pieces or repair destroyed objects, and it can also counteract later possession or curse effects.

Worm Prophet has an actual Mending spell item associated with Divine Prepared Spells, and its ID is prepared in a 1st-rank slot. Mending repairs item HP and can remove broken, but at this low rank the actor has a narrow repair capability and cannot fix missing pieces or destroyed objects.

Vault Builder has Mending associated with Arcane Prepared Spells and prepared in a 3rd-rank slot, so the actor can directly repair small objects (including a nonmagical object up to 2 Bulk or a magical object up to 1 Bulk). The spell restores 5 HP per rank and can clear broken, but cannot replace missing pieces or repair destroyed objects.

Broken defines the state and penalties for damaged objects, but does not restore object Hit Points or describe any repair method; it is useful condition context rather than an answer that repairs objects.
This spell removes the area's air and steals creatures' breath; on a critical failure it immediately starts suffocation, the reverse of surviving without air.
It protects against severe or extreme temperatures, but its stated protection does not address breathing or absent air.
The spell creates a replenishing shell of fresh air and explicitly lets the target breathe in a vacuum, directly meeting the intent.

Austral has an At Will Air Bubble spell associated with its Divine Innate Spells entry; that spell puts pure air around a target's head so it can breathe normally. This is a directly useful but spell-limited creature answer.
The feat extends how long its user can hold their breath, so it can help endure a short airless interval, but it does not supply air or remove the need to breathe.
Subsist concerns finding food and shelter in an environment; it provides no way to breathe or endure missing air.
This feat improves downtime Subsist checks and access in unusual environments, but says nothing about breathing or airless survival.

Fumbus has the Breath Control feat, which greatly extends breath-holding and improves saves against inhaled dangers. It only delays suffocation rather than providing breathable air or removing the need to breathe.
The cave-in hazard damages and immobilizes creatures and blocks a tunnel; it does not help anyone breathe or survive an airless environment.
This is an actual fire spell, but the record is the spell itself rather than a caster characterized by fire magic.
The spell uses fire for its teleportation route, but it is not a caster record and does not establish a fire-magic character.
Wildfire is a fire-damaging focus spell, but this record supplies an individual spell rather than the caster requested.

The clockwork mage has an Arcane Innate Spells entry linked to Wall of Fire, so it can cast fire magic; its source description characterizes it broadly as a magically powered machine, making fire a qualified rather than dominant theme.

This is a fire elemental described as a walking conflagration, with fire attacks and fire abilities, but the source presents no spellcasting entry or spell capability; it is related to fire magic without being a caster answer.

The watchmage is an arcane prepared caster and has Ignition linked to its prepared-spell entry and listed in a prepared slot. That provides real fire magic, but the source characterizes the watchmage around law enforcement and offers only this fire cantrip among its spells.

The magma dragon has both innate fire spells and numerous prepared fire spells, including Fire Seeds, Flame Strike, Wall of Fire, Produce Flame, and Burning Hands. Its volcanic lair and magma-dragon identity reinforce a strong fire-magic characterization.

The witchfire has occult innate and coven spells, but the listed spell set does not establish fire casting. Its sickly green witchflame is a magical feature and fire-themed, yet that makes it a related spirit rather than a fire caster.

This mercenary wizard has prepared Flaming Sphere, Burning Hands, and Produce Flame, all linked to its Prepared Arcane Spells entry and listed in spell slots. Multiple usable fire spells make it a direct fire-mage answer despite its generic mercenary characterization.

The Chelaxian mage has multiple fire spells prepared in its Arcane Prepared Spells entry, including Fireball, Blazing Bolt, Breathe Fire, and Ignition; its Brimstone Blessing also channels devilish energy into fire damage. This is a direct caster answer.
Insect Form transforms its caster into an insect battle form; it does not call insects or insect swarms forth, so it is related to insects but does not meet the summoning intent.

The priest has Vomit Swarm linked to its Occult Innate Spells entry. The spell explicitly evokes a magical swarm including centipedes, roaches, wasps, and worms, directly calling forth insects and other vermin.

The zebub has an innate Summon Animal spell explicitly limited to swarm creatures, so it can call a swarm to fight. The spell's generic animal wording does not establish that a particular insect swarm is the one selected, making this a qualified answer.

This creature is made of worms and can collapse into a worm swarm, but the authored intent explicitly excludes merely existing as a swarm. Its listed Summon Entity summons an aberration, while Visions of Danger only creates illusory swarming monsters that deal mental damage.

The Bee-Man has a Primal Innate Spells entry with a linked Summon Animal spell specifically restricted to bee swarms treated as wasp swarms; it can therefore call insect swarms to fight. The spell has three uses, which is a practical limit but does not make this direct answer indirect.

Azvalvigander has an innate Summon Animal spell limited to swarm creatures and can call such a swarm to fight. Because the spell is not restricted specifically to insect swarms, its fit is useful but qualified.

The jorogumo disciple's innate Summon Animal spell is restricted to spiders, not insects. That is a related arthropod summoning capability but does not meet the requested insect or insect-swarm target.

The philosophy concerns undeath and transition after death, so it is broadly related to souls and life/death, but it provides no Jistka, construct, or ancestry lore and cannot answer how those constructs house souls.

The journal contains a clearly identified Automaton page. It explains that the Jistkan Artificer Conclave created automatons by transplanting the mind, life force, and soul of Jistkan individuals into constructs, directly answering the request.

Saloc's lore concerns souls in the afterlife and the deity may resurrect condemned souls, but it gives no Jistka or construct ancestry explanation. It is related to souls but does not answer the query.

Excise Lexicon prevents the target from registering or understanding selected words in any form, even through tongues. It is directly about language comprehension but reverses the requested ability for those words.
Truespeech lets its target understand all words regardless of language and speak in a language each listener understands, directly enabling cross-language comprehension and communication.
The rooftop guardian has a constant Truespeech effect linked to its Occult Innate Spells entry; it can understand all languages and speak in languages other creatures understand.
Avsheros has a constant Tongues spell linked to its Divine Innate Spells entry, granting universal comprehension and the ability to speak languages its listeners understand.

The aiuvarin translator is specifically presented as a translator and gets a +5 bonus to checks involving translation or deciphering languages. This is useful help crossing language barriers, although it requires checks and does not grant automatic understanding or speech in every language.

Vixivax has Truespeech linked to its Divine Innate Spells entry; the spell directly grants all-language understanding and listener-matched speech. At its listed 5th-rank casting the duration is one hour, so the capability is direct with a bounded duration.
The locus haunt causes mental confusion and compels destructive behavior, but its hazard actions contain no music or damaging performance.

The lorekeeper is a storyteller and has a castable Noise Blast that damages and deafens listeners, but that spell produces cacophonous noise rather than a musical performance. Its speech-or-song spell, Enthrall, only fascinates targets, so the record does not establish injurious music.
Fatal Shot is a weapon attack that can kill its target, but it has no music, sound, or performance component.

Arika is a bard with musical composition magic, and has castable Noise Blast spells that harm and deafen listeners. However, those blasts are described as cacophonous noise, not music or a performance; her actual song effects instead protect allies or bolster them.
Unkillable prevents its user from reaching 0 HP after a potentially fatal blow; it contains no music or effect that harms listeners.

Taljjae is not a spirit or ghost: its source traits identify it as fey. Its signature masks are nevertheless central to its characterization, and it repeatedly removes and dons them to change characters, making it a useful masked-entity alternative with the spirit aspect unmet.

This source is a supernatural Mask of Norgorber, created when a worshipper is transformed into a mask proxy. It is a direct masked entity, but its source traits identify it as a fiendish humanoid rather than a spirit or ghost, so it is a qualified alternative.

The feat makes a mask into a familiar with its own personality; it can detach into a moving body of colored light and speaks in a distinct voice. That is a useful supernatural mask-entity, but the source does not characterize the familiar as a ghost or spirit.
This record is a magical mask with breathing protections and a breath-stealing activation, but the item itself is not a spirit or ghost and is not characterized as an entity.
The lich is a creature record carrying a Staff of Fire (Greater), a different canonical staff rank from the requested Major staff. Shared staff-family identity does not answer the exact rank lookup.
Atmospheric Staff (Major) is a different canonical staff with air and gravity spells, not Staff of Fire (Major). The shared staff type and Major rank do not make it the requested identity.
Fluid Form Staff (Major) is a different canonical staff focused on morph and polymorph spells, not the requested Staff of Fire (Major).

The Eldritch Emeritus carries an actual, held +2 Greater Striking Staff of Fire (Major), with the staff's spell list embedded in the actor record. This is useful evidence of the requested staff identity, though the result is a creature with a rune-enhanced instance rather than the canonical standalone equipment record.
The 3rd-level permanent-items table lists a Staff of Fire, but it omits the Major rank requested. It helps locate the staff family, not the exact canonical variant.
Staff of Fire (Greater) is a different canonical rank from Staff of Fire (Major), so it is not a useful exact-name answer despite sharing the base staff identity.

The 12th-level permanent-items table includes an exact Staff of Fire (Major) row and a direct equipment document ID, which is useful for resolving the canonical identity. The table row is still an index entry rather than the full equipment document.
The greater staff has the requested ignition behavior and lists Fireball among its charge-castable spells; it directly answers the item lookup.
This staff ignites tinder, but its spell list contains only Ignition and Breathe Fire, not Fireball or Wall of Fire; it supplies one distinctive behavior while missing the requested spell capability.
These are consumable pellets that augment a separately cast Fireball with persistent damage; they are not a staff and have no tinder-ignition function.

Ilgreth is not a root record named Fly, but its prepared Arcane Spells entry currently includes the exact rank-4 Fly spell, so the creature has a usable flight capability; it is a related copied-spell record, not the requested name identity.

Sonnorae is a velstrac, not a root record named Fly; its linked innate Fly (Constant) spell provides flight, making this a useful capability association but a copied creature spell rather than the exact name identity.
Irovetti is a creature record with the exact Fly spell in his spontaneous occult repertoire and available rank-4 slots; he is a castable-spell owner, not the root record named Fly.
Aerial Form is a different canonical spell that transforms the caster into a flying animal; shared flight function does not make it the exact Fly spell or action identity.
Arboreal sapstrikers are woodland beings whose forest guides their purpose, and they track down and punish loggers, a specific protective behavior rather than mere forest residence.

Waldgeists are explicitly formed from destroyed trees and become guardians of a forest; their Forest Guardian action compels them to investigate tree damage, while their bond limits them to one woodland.
Arboreal regents are explicitly responsible for guarding an entire forest and gather to plan against grave regional threats, directly matching both entity and stewardship.

This fiendish arboreal is a forest-patrolling warden: the source says wardens scout their woodland for threats and report dangers to regents, while arboreals are guardians of the forest. Its fiendish trait does not remove that protective role.

The student is explicitly described as a sorcerous monk and has multiple owned cold spells in its spontaneous arcane repertoire, including Polar Ray, Ray of Frost, and Wall of Ice. Its Bludgeoning Energy feature changes energy damage to bludgeoning, so the damaging effects do not retain cold damage, but the record still directly identifies a sorcerous caster with several cold spells and ice magic.

The Frostripper has an actual Primal innate spellcasting entry with multiple directly owned cold spells, including Howling Blizzard, Wall of Ice, and Frostbite, rather than merely a cold breath or environmental association. This is a creature using cold spellcasting and therefore a comparable caster for the authored intent.

Animal Pit is itself a weight-activated hidden pit trap: its description says a trap door covers a 10-by-20-foot pit, has a stealth DC, and the owned Pitfall action makes a triggering creature fall in. The named root is Animal Pit, but the owned action supplies the trap behavior for navigation.

Unstable Pit is an environmental pit hazard with a trap reaction that can make a creature slide into the pit, so it is useful for the pit portion of the intent. Its source explicitly says the formerly covered pit is now visible; only the unstable edge is not obvious, making it a qualified rather than a direct hidden-pit match.

The complex Riotous Mushrooms hazard’s routine directs an adjacent mushroom to use Poison Spores, which deals nonlethal poison damage to adjacent creatures. This is a useful environmental poison-spore exposure, but the source does not describe a gas cloud or say the spores disperse through the air, so it is a qualified match to poisonous gas.

The mask has Toxic Cloud linked to its Divine Innate Spells entry; the spell creates poisonous fog and deals poison damage to every breathing creature that starts its turn in the area. Its separate once-daily Evaporate Poison action can also turn an affliction into toxic vapor that exposes nearby creatures to brimstone fumes.

The Scarlet Triad Agent owns poisons and hollow blowgun darts for delivery, so it is substantively related to poison use. The source describes the Lethargy Poison and Purple Worm Venom as injury poisons activated by Interact; neither this equipment nor the agent’s listed mechanics expose people to poisonous gas.

Mother Venom’s spontaneous divine spell repertoire includes Stinking Cloud, a rank-3 poison-trait cloud of putrid mist that sickens creatures ending turns inside it. The linked spellcasting entry has rank-3 slots, so this is an owned gas-like poison effect available to the creature, not merely the unrelated venom in its melee poison item.

Gas Trap explicitly seals the room and pumps poison gas through four hidden vents. Its routine deals poison damage to breathing creatures each round and identifies blocking all vents as the way to disable it, a direct environmental poisonous-gas threat.

Befuddling Gas Trap is an environmental hazard whose description says seven concealed ceiling nozzles release poison gas when the room is closed with a creature inside. The gas causes stupefaction and mental damage rather than poison damage, but the authored intent does not require a specific damage type or saving-throw result.

Seoni directly owns a Lesser Antidote, the requested poison-protection consumable, with its one-use inventory quantity. The minor Elixir of Life is an additional poison-save aid, but the antidote alone makes this a direct equipment result.

Keznin carries two Moderate Antidotes, which protect against poisons, so this is a direct consumable match regardless of the requested dose tier. His expanded healer’s tools and Expert Herbalist action also support Treat Poison, but those are additional medical capabilities rather than the basis for the direct grade.

Yacob carries a Lesser Antidote, a direct poison-protection consumable, with one use recorded in the inventory. His healer’s tools support Treat Poison as a separate medical capability, but the owned antidote itself directly satisfies the equipment/consumable discovery intent.

Open the Wall of Ghosts is a ritual that opens the specifically named Wall of Ghosts and allows other creatures to pass through it. That is an actual passage through a barrier, but it applies to this singular supernatural wall and requires a day-long ritual at the specified lunar time, so it is a constrained route rather than a general wall-crossing answer.

Door to Beyond creates cracks that pull creatures toward a breach in reality, so it is substantively related to barriers and passage. Its description explicitly says the cracks are too thin for anything to fully slip through; it therefore cannot transport a creature through a wall or open a passable doorway.

The Annis Hag has Passwall in its Coven Spells casting entry, with a rank-5 innate slot and the spell linked to that entry. Passwall creates a tunnel through a wall that creatures can move through; this is a direct wall-crossing capability, with its source-record coven context stated rather than assumed away.

Darivan is explicitly a sorcerer, and his spontaneous Primal Spells entry includes Passwall linked at rank 5 with rank-5 spell slots. The spell creates a traversable tunnel through a wall, making this a direct match to passing through a solid barrier.

Hunter’s Anthem is a longbow, but its Song of the Bow damages nearby creatures with sonic damage; it supplies no healing effect or creature owner.
The trumpet archon has Heal and Breath of Life for allies, but the owned weapon is a bastard sword and no bow is present.
Coerce is a minute-long Intimidation check that compels a creature to comply; it has no attack, reaction, or opportunity trigger corresponding to the old action.
Accidental Shot is a ranged Strike with a fortune benefit, so it is attack-related, but it is a once-daily action rather than a reaction to an opening.
A Moment Unending adds precision damage to a later Strike, making it substantively attack-related, but it has no reaction or triggering enemy action.

Reactive Strike is the source-verified renamed action: its reaction triggers when a nearby creature moves, manipulates, or makes a ranged attack, then makes a melee Strike and can disrupt a critical-hit manipulate action.
Foresight is a reaction to a target defending against danger, but it changes roll outcomes rather than making the counterattack that defined Attack of Opportunity.
Trip is an attack-trait maneuver against a creature’s Reflex DC; it is related to combat attacks but is not a reactive strike or old-name alias.
Escape removes grabbed, immobilized, or restrained conditions by checking against their source; its attack trait applies to the check, not to an opportunity attack.
Calculate Threats grants AC and Reflex bonuses against incoming attacks, a defense-related response but not the old action’s reactive Strike.
Overload Vision reacts when a creature attacks the user and can dazzle or blind it, so it is attack-triggered but does not make the requested counterattack.
Devise a Stratagem helps plan an attack roll against a chosen foe, but it is an action before the Strike rather than a reaction to an opening.
Exploit Vulnerability identifies a foe’s weakness and empowers later Strikes; that is combat-attack support, not an opportunity reaction or renamed action.
Strike is the basic attack used by Reactive Strike, but this generic action has no reaction, trigger, or old-name identity on its own.
Flyby Attack combines flight with a Strike, making it movement-and-attack related, but it is a two-action activity rather than a reaction to an enemy opening.
Amassed Assault damages enemies in a companion’s space, so it is a substantive offensive action but not a reactive single Strike or the renamed rule.
Threatening Approach is a Stride followed by Demoralize; its effects concern frightened, not attacks or reactions.
Opportunistic Accusation is a reaction that damages a demon after a specific vulnerability or save failure, but it does not counterattack a creature’s movement or manipulate opening.
Boarding Assault moves or swings and then makes a Strike; it is an attack after movement, not a reaction to an opponent’s movement.
Impromptu Investment swaps invested items over a minute and has no attack, reaction, or opportunity mechanic.
Opportune Riposte is a genuine reaction Strike, but its trigger is a foe critically failing a Strike against you, not the old action’s movement, manipulate, or ranged-attack triggers.
Feint sets up a later melee attack by making the target off-guard; it is attack-related but has no reaction or trigger matching Attack of Opportunity.
Sense Weakness is a reaction that makes a dueling opponent off-guard against an imminent melee Strike, but it modifies an attack instead of making an opportunity Strike.
Force Open can smash doors or walls with Athletics, but that object-breaking action is unrelated to the old reaction attack.
Inspired Stratagem is a reaction before an ally’s attack roll that grants fortune, so it is attack-roll related but does not counterattack or match the renamed action.

Implement’s Interruption is the closest qualified analogue: under Exploit Vulnerability and weapon-implement requirements it reacts to move, manipulate, or concentrate actions with a Strike and possible disruption, but it is a separate restricted feature rather than the renamed general action.
The snake is an electricity-themed creature with static attacks and a lightning strike that redirects energy absorbed from storms; those attacks do not make its body or identity a storm.
This is directly a living cloud: its authored description calls it a humanoid-shaped storm cloud, and its innate thunderbolt attack makes the storm embodiment concrete.
The metal sphere is a magnetic elemental; it reverses polarity when struck by electricity, but its active field manipulates metal rather than embodying or creating a storm.
This feat helps a character function in bad weather and grants no storm form or storm-producing power; weather familiarity is related but does not answer with an entity.
The hazard is a magical rune trap that releases void and sonic damage when someone approaches; thunder is only its roar, not a storm entity or storm manifestation.

This air elemental is itself a swirling dust-devil-like whirlwind, with a high-winds aura and an action that creates violent wind; the identity and mechanics both embody storm-like air.
The rune is a constructed magical symbol, and its electricity attack is an energy-damage option; neither the identity nor the authored abilities make it a storm.
This autonomous rune can make an electrical blast, but its authored identity is a constructed written symbol and it has no storm embodiment or weather ability.
The source describes a connected grove of trees and plant-elemental behavior; the wind phrase occurs only in a camouflage effect ending, with no storm concept fit.
The storm lord is an air elemental explicitly identified with battles on the Plane of Air; its high-winds aura and lightning lash are built-in stormlike powers.

This is a useful constrained living-rain alternative: the swarm consists of storm-born creatures made when magical energy and rainfall transform the droplets into life, though the swarm is not itself a weather system.

The creature is an animate dream formed from dream fragments and fear. Thunderstrike is mentioned only as an example of a spell a designer might optionally choose, not as an actual storm power of this record.
Agyra is titled the Forever Storm and can generate a four-mile hurricane centered on herself; this is an explicit storm manifestation by the entity, alongside her lightning abilities.
This is another animated flat-surface painting; the blood-themed healing interaction and paint attacks do not supply any storm identity or capability.
The living waterfall is a humanoid column of churning water with aquatic vortex effects; it is a water elemental rather than a storm embodiment, though its flowing-water nature is related.
This background concerns surviving a maritime disaster and gaining weather sense and Weather Lore; it provides no entity or storm manifestation.

Sthira is an undead assemblage rather than a storm creature, but the actor has an associated primal innate-spell entry and a linked Storm of Vengeance spell, constrained here to hail each round; that is a useful storm-casting route.
The oil graffiti source describes a magically animated drawing restricted to flat surfaces; the oil/pigment theme has no storm connection.
This hazard creates a real lightning-and-tornado storm, but it is an environmental encounter hazard with a triggered event, not an entity embodying or manifesting as a storm.

Jesseri is not herself a storm, but her linked spontaneous primal repertoire includes Ice Storm and other weather effects such as wind and lightning; this is a useful spellcaster alternative, not an embodied storm.

The archer is a fey hunter whose hair moves in a gentle breeze; this is incidental atmosphere, while its listed cloudkill effect is poisonous fog, not storm embodiment.

Iogaka is explicitly a storm hag personifying a storm’s rage; its stormcalling ability can create hurricanes, thunderstorms, or tornadoes regardless of season.
Austral is an anemos whose true form is coalesced wind, and the source says cardinal anemoi direct world-spanning winds; this is an entity embodied as moving air.
The storm hag is expressly called the personification of a storm’s rage, and its stormcalling power actively creates severe weather; it directly answers the entity intent.
The hazard’s triggered effect is a wind-and-fire storm that throws debris and sharp rain, but the record is a nonliving hazard event rather than a storm entity.
This elemental embodies molten magma and volcanic eruptions, a fire/earth phenomenon rather than a storm or weather entity.
This living rune can cast Chain Lightning, but its source identity is a constructed glyph and its lightning is a spell attack rather than storm embodiment or weather power.
The giant’s prose says it embodies tempest fury and the calm of a hurricane’s eye; it also has at-will Control Weather, so its storm identity is backed by usable weather power.
This is a general archetypes journal. The cited [quotation omitted] language is a metaphor for a dual-weapon fighting style and the entry describes weapon attacks, not a living or manifesting storm.
The spell directly creates a cloud with selectable rain, wind, or fog and allows repeated lightning strikes, so it is a useful spell-level storm manifestation; it is not itself a living entity.
This is a magically animated chalk drawing that moves on flat surfaces; chalk and paint effects provide no storm connection.

Tormonshilds are living creatures literally formed from raindrops during artificially created storms, a constrained rain-born living alternative though the resulting frog-like individual is not itself a storm system.
This higher-level variant is still a nonliving hazard whose triggered storm of wind and fire attacks an area; it is related to storm manifestation but does not answer with an entity.

This is an earth-plane herd animal made of rock and metal; its description and abilities involve gliding through earth, not storm or weather.
This rule defines when an object is broken and what that state does, but it does not perform or provide a repair method. It is directly related context, not a useful repair answer.
Restore Ground destroys unattended objects while returning land to nature, so its object effect reverses the requested repair function rather than restoring damaged items.
Haphazard Repair lets an inventor quickly repair only their own innovation, and still requires adjacency and a repair kit; it is a useful but narrowly scoped repair option.

Community Repair restores a damaged public work to its prior construction and function, but it requires a community ritual with connected anecdotes and automatically fails if a caster intentionally destroyed the work.
Item Facade makes a broken object look and feel intact but does not restore HP or its actual function, so it supplies an illusion of repair rather than repairing the object.

Kyra is a cleric whose actual Fire domain focus spell, Fire Ray, attacks with a blazing band and deals fire damage; her source also describes Sarenrae’s fire-centered doctrine. This is a creature with an intrinsic fire ability, not merely an incidental item mention.

Burning Building is itself a hazard with the fire trait, and its Conflagration action damages occupants with fire while Spread propagates the burning condition to another building; this directly fits the broad fire discovery intent.

This young Fortune Dragon actor contains a real Fireball spell item, heightened to 5th rank and owned by its Arcane Spontaneous Spells entry with one 5th-rank slot. That is useful evidence of a creature carrying the spell, while the actor record is not the canonical spell document.

Firestarter Pellets are a consumable catalyst whose description says they modify a Fireball spell; the record is useful adjacent equipment context, but it is neither the spell nor a creature that owns it.

Greater Fireball Rune is a hazard whose Fireball action explicitly casts a 4th-rank Fireball spell for fire damage. This is a useful source for a Fireball effect, but the hazard record is not the canonical named spell document.

Koto Zekora’s actor owns two Fireball spell items, at 3rd and 5th rank, both associated with its Spontaneous Arcane Spells entry and the corresponding slots. The copied spells make this useful under an unfiltered query, though the actor is not the canonical spell document.

Tupilaq owns a Fireball spell item associated with Primal Innate Spells; its record gives a 3rd-rank spell heightened to 3rd with three innate uses. Under the explicit creature filter, the owner is an intentional useful match, even though this is not the canonical spell record.

Emriss’s actor contains a 3rd-rank Fireball spell associated with Divine Spontaneous Spells and a 3rd-rank slot. This directly identifies a creature that owns the spell for the filtered query, while remaining an actor record.

Asper Hajeri’s actor contains a 3rd-rank Fireball spell associated with Primal Spontaneous Spells and a 3rd-rank slot. This is useful under the creature filter because the actor owns the requested spell, though it is not the canonical spell document.

Arrogant Entodemonologist has a Fireball item tied to its Arcane Prepared Spells entry, and that entry’s 3rd-rank prepared slot contains the spell item ID. This is a direct filtered creature owner, not the canonical spell record.

The adult Fortune Dragon owns Fireball through Arcane Spontaneous Spells; this actor’s copy is heightened to 7th rank and associated with its 7th-rank slots. It is useful for a creature-filtered search but is not the canonical spell document.

This second Fortune Dragon (Young) actor record also owns the 3rd-rank Fireball item, heightened to 5th through its Arcane Spontaneous Spells entry. It is useful owner evidence, while the duplicate actor source is not the canonical spell document.

Barralbus’s complete actor item list contains an Arcane Prepared Spells entry and fire spells such as Produce Flame and Flaming Sphere, but no Fireball spell item or Fireball prepared slot. Fire-themed magic alone does not answer the exact Fireball query.

Lightlock is a magical room trap whose F8 trigger fires chilling dark fog at a creature carrying light; the action deals 10d6 cold damage and is explicitly named [quotation omitted] It directly fits a room-wide cold hazard, although it does not literally freeze victims.

Boreal Rage Trap operates in a room: it triggers when a creature enters marked areas or remains there for one minute, then breathes cold over a 15-foot burst; a critical failure causes frostbite. This directly fits a room hazard with cold/freeze effects.

Flooding Room is an enclosed mechanical trap that seals the room and eventually fills it with river water, but its full description gives falling-water bludgeoning damage rather than any cold or freezing effect. The room-hazard facet matches while the key effect is missing.
Familiar of Freezing Rime describes a familiar whose cold breath creates ice and difficult terrain, but it is a familiar rule rather than an enclosed room hazard and does not freeze room occupants.
Dead Faine is a living human with an occult spell that can mimic undead, but its source shows ordinary padded armor and no ghost, possession, or curse associated with that armor.

Lightweight Animated Armor is itself armor animated as a mindless construct through rituals or strange magic; it is a useful supernatural animated-armor alternative, but its source does not identify a haunting, possessing spirit, or curse.
Hansin is a living human gang leader carrying ordinary studded leather armor; the source provides no haunting, possession, or curse attached to either the creature or its armor.

Accursed Forge-Spurned is an undead dwarf in ordinary Full Plate, and its cursed item is a soul chain rather than the armor. That is related undead-and-armor context but does not provide haunted or cursed armor.

Animated Armor (BB) is a mindless construct whose source says suits of armor are animated by rituals or strange magic; it is a useful animated-armor supernatural alternative, though not specifically haunted, possessed, or cursed.

Graveknight’s Curse applies to anyone who wears a graveknight’s armor for at least an hour, prevents removal, and ultimately kills and transforms the wearer into the armor’s graveknight. This directly describes a cursed armor relationship.

Singing Shortbow is a real composite shortbow whose Song of Soothing restores 5d10 Hit Points to nearby creatures; it supplies both the bow and a healing effect, but the equipment record does not identify a creature owner who uses it.
Heal Companion restores Hit Points to an animal companion, so it is the healing half of the query, but this standalone spell record names no creature owner or bow use.
Feiya can heal others with her Occult Prepared Soothe spell and also carries a Crossbow; both capabilities belong to her character, but her listed weapon is a crossbow rather than a bow.
Staff of Healing (Major) has Heal among the spells it can cast, but it is only a staff item record and does not identify a creature owner or any bow.
Tsimaan has Medicine skill and expanded healer’s tools to perform healing checks, and owns a Crossbow; the same creature has healing and a similar ranged weapon, but the weapon is not a bow.
Dewey Daystar has an innate Heal spell and a Wand of Heal, so the actor can restore other creatures’ Hit Points; its complete inventory contains no bow, leaving the second requested capability unmet.

Lantern Archon owns a Heal spell associated with Divine Innate Spells, which can restore Hit Points to a willing living target; the creature record contains no bow, so it supplies only the healer side.

Stone-Breasted Owl has a primal innate Heal spell with two uses, and its Empowered Healing action increases the spell’s healing die; its inventory has no bow, so it does not meet the combined request.

Shalelu Andosana’s Soothing Mist is a healing focus spell that restores 2d8 Hit Points to a living target, associated with her Ranger Warden spellcasting entry and backed by three current focus points. The same actor carries Hunter’s Anthem, a longbow, and arrows, so the source shows both requested capabilities on her; its item state says worn with no hands held, so current wielding is not established.

Devise a Stratagem is an investigator action that assesses a foe and substitutes a previously rolled d20 for a Strike or skill check; its source contains no Attack of Opportunity name, old-name note, or reaction attack. It is a different action, so it does not answer the renamed-action lookup.

Venomfist is a water elemental whose own presence changes the weather over two miles to heavy rainfall, and its hostility turns nearby rain into a damaging toxic downpour. Its innate spell list also includes Wrathful Storm, an actual storm cloud with rain and gales. These are owned, active storm manifestations rather than incidental lightning vocabulary.

Diskah Night Watcher is a humanoid druid, not a storm being, but she owns usable storm-casting: Howling Blizzard is prepared in her 5th-rank Primal slot, and Tempest Surge is a Druidic Order focus spell with two focus points available. This is a useful storm-capable owner, while the record does not portray her as an embodied storm.
Living Boulder is an earth elemental that rolls across the Plane of Earth and glides through rock; its own description and abilities contain no storm, wind, rain, or lightning embodiment.

Living Graffiti (Chalk) is a construct painting that moves across flat surfaces and attacks with chalk; the source includes no storm manifestation or weather power. Its incidental Fireball reference only describes a way to destroy the surface it inhabits.
Storm Born is a druid feat that protects its bearer from penalties caused by weather and concealment in fog; it grants weather resilience, not a storm identity or a power to manifest storms.

Rite of Repatriation explicitly repairs damage to a culturally important object and can restore up to 5 Hit Points per ritual rank, potentially clearing broken. Its use is sharply limited: only damage since the rightful owners last possessed it qualifies, spirits must accept, it cannot replace missing pieces or repair destroyed objects, and it can also counteract later possession or curse effects.

Worm Prophet has an actual Mending spell item associated with Divine Prepared Spells, and its ID is prepared in a 1st-rank slot. Mending repairs item HP and can remove broken, but at this low rank the actor has a narrow repair capability and cannot fix missing pieces or destroyed objects.

Vault Builder has Mending associated with Arcane Prepared Spells and prepared in a 3rd-rank slot, so the actor can directly repair small objects (including a nonmagical object up to 2 Bulk or a magical object up to 1 Bulk). The spell restores 5 HP per rank and can clear broken, but cannot replace missing pieces or repair destroyed objects.

Broken defines the state and penalties for damaged objects, but does not restore object Hit Points or describe any repair method; it is useful condition context rather than an answer that repairs objects.
This spell removes the area's air and steals creatures' breath; on a critical failure it immediately starts suffocation, the reverse of surviving without air.
It protects against severe or extreme temperatures, but its stated protection does not address breathing or absent air.
The spell creates a replenishing shell of fresh air and explicitly lets the target breathe in a vacuum, directly meeting the intent.

Austral has an At Will Air Bubble spell associated with its Divine Innate Spells entry; that spell puts pure air around a target's head so it can breathe normally. This is a directly useful but spell-limited creature answer.
The feat extends how long its user can hold their breath, so it can help endure a short airless interval, but it does not supply air or remove the need to breathe.

Insect Form transforms its caster into an insect battle form; it does not call insects or insect swarms forth, so it is related to insects but does not meet the summoning intent.

The priest has Vomit Swarm linked to its Occult Innate Spells entry. The spell explicitly evokes a magical swarm including centipedes, roaches, wasps, and worms, directly calling forth insects and other vermin.

The zebub has an innate Summon Animal spell explicitly limited to swarm creatures, so it can call a swarm to fight. The spell's generic animal wording does not establish that a particular insect swarm is the one selected, making this a qualified answer.

This creature is made of worms and can collapse into a worm swarm, but the authored intent explicitly excludes merely existing as a swarm. Its listed Summon Entity summons an aberration, while Visions of Danger only creates illusory swarming monsters that deal mental damage.

The Bee-Man has a Primal Innate Spells entry with a linked Summon Animal spell specifically restricted to bee swarms treated as wasp swarms; it can therefore call insect swarms to fight. The spell has three uses, which is a practical limit but does not make this direct answer indirect.

Azvalvigander has an innate Summon Animal spell limited to swarm creatures and can call such a swarm to fight. Because the spell is not restricted specifically to insect swarms, its fit is useful but qualified.

The jorogumo disciple's innate Summon Animal spell is restricted to spiders, not insects. That is a related arthropod summoning capability but does not meet the requested insect or insect-swarm target.

The philosophy concerns undeath and transition after death, so it is broadly related to souls and life/death, but it provides no Jistka, construct, or ancestry lore and cannot answer how those constructs house souls.

The journal contains a clearly identified Automaton page. It explains that the Jistkan Artificer Conclave created automatons by transplanting the mind, life force, and soul of Jistkan individuals into constructs, directly answering the request.

Saloc's lore concerns souls in the afterlife and the deity may resurrect condemned souls, but it gives no Jistka or construct ancestry explanation. It is related to souls but does not answer the query.

Excise Lexicon prevents the target from registering or understanding selected words in any form, even through tongues. It is directly about language comprehension but reverses the requested ability for those words.
Truespeech lets its target understand all words regardless of language and speak in a language each listener understands, directly enabling cross-language comprehension and communication.
The rooftop guardian has a constant Truespeech effect linked to its Occult Innate Spells entry; it can understand all languages and speak in languages other creatures understand.
Avsheros has a constant Tongues spell linked to its Divine Innate Spells entry, granting universal comprehension and the ability to speak languages its listeners understand.

The aiuvarin translator is specifically presented as a translator and gets a +5 bonus to checks involving translation or deciphering languages. This is useful help crossing language barriers, although it requires checks and does not grant automatic understanding or speech in every language.

Vixivax has Truespeech linked to its Divine Innate Spells entry; the spell directly grants all-language understanding and listener-matched speech. At its listed 5th-rank casting the duration is one hour, so the capability is direct with a bounded duration.
The locus haunt causes mental confusion and compels destructive behavior, but its hazard actions contain no music or damaging performance.

The lorekeeper is a storyteller and has a castable Noise Blast that damages and deafens listeners, but that spell produces cacophonous noise rather than a musical performance. Its speech-or-song spell, Enthrall, only fascinates targets, so the record does not establish injurious music.
Fatal Shot is a weapon attack that can kill its target, but it has no music, sound, or performance component.

Arika is a bard with musical composition magic, and has castable Noise Blast spells that harm and deafen listeners. However, those blasts are described as cacophonous noise, not music or a performance; her actual song effects instead protect allies or bolster them.
Unkillable prevents its user from reaching 0 HP after a potentially fatal blow; it contains no music or effect that harms listeners.

Taljjae is not a spirit or ghost: its source traits identify it as fey. Its signature masks are nevertheless central to its characterization, and it repeatedly removes and dons them to change characters, making it a useful masked-entity alternative with the spirit aspect unmet.

This source is a supernatural Mask of Norgorber, created when a worshipper is transformed into a mask proxy. It is a direct masked entity, but its source traits identify it as a fiendish humanoid rather than a spirit or ghost, so it is a qualified alternative.

The feat makes a mask into a familiar with its own personality; it can detach into a moving body of colored light and speaks in a distinct voice. That is a useful supernatural mask-entity, but the source does not characterize the familiar as a ghost or spirit.
This record is a magical mask with breathing protections and a breath-stealing activation, but the item itself is not a spirit or ghost and is not characterized as an entity.

Atmospheric Staff (Major) is a different canonical staff with air and gravity spells, not Staff of Fire (Major). The shared staff type and Major rank do not make it the requested identity.
Fluid Form Staff (Major) is a different canonical staff focused on morph and polymorph spells, not the requested Staff of Fire (Major).

The Eldritch Emeritus carries an actual, held +2 Greater Striking Staff of Fire (Major), with the staff's spell list embedded in the actor record. The 3rd-level permanent-items table lists a Staff of Fire, but it omits the Major rank requested. It helps locate the staff family, not the exact canonical variant.
Staff of Fire (Greater) is a different canonical rank from Staff of Fire (Major), so it is not a useful exact-name answer despite sharing the base staff identity.

The 12th-level permanent-items table includes an exact Staff of Fire (Major) row and a direct equipment document ID, which is useful for resolving the canonical identity. The table row is still an index entry rather than the full equipment document.
The greater staff has the requested ignition behavior and lists Fireball among its charge-castable spells; it directly answers the item lookup.
This staff ignites tinder, but its spell list contains only Ignition and Breathe Fire, not Fireball or Wall of Fire; it supplies one distinctive behavior while missing the requested spell capability.
These are consumable pellets that augment a separately cast Fireball with persistent damage; they are not a staff and have no tinder-ignition function.

Ilgreth is not a root record named Fly, but its prepared Arcane Spells entry currently includes the exact rank-4 Fly spell, so the creature has a usable flight capability; it is a related copied-spell record, not the requested name identity.

Sonnorae is a velstrac, not a root record named Fly; its linked innate Fly (Constant) spell provides flight, making this a useful capability association but a copied creature spell rather than the exact name identity.
Irovetti is a creature record with the exact Fly spell in his spontaneous occult repertoire and available rank-4 slots; he is a castable-spell owner, not the root record named Fly.
Aerial Form is a different canonical spell that transforms the caster into a flying animal; shared flight function does not make it the exact Fly spell or action identity.
Arboreal sapstrikers are woodland beings whose forest guides their purpose, and they track down and punish loggers, a specific protective behavior rather than mere forest residence.

Waldgeists are explicitly formed from destroyed trees and become guardians of a forest; their Forest Guardian action compels them to investigate tree damage, while their bond limits them to one woodland.
Arboreal regents are explicitly responsible for guarding an entire forest and gather to plan against grave regional threats, directly matching both entity and stewardship.

This fiendish arboreal is a forest-patrolling warden: the source says wardens scout their woodland for threats and report dangers to regents, while arboreals are guardians of the forest. Its fiendish trait does not remove that protective role.

The student is explicitly described as a sorcerous monk and has multiple owned cold spells in its spontaneous arcane repertoire, including Polar Ray, Ray of Frost, and Wall of Ice. Its Bludgeoning Energy feature changes energy damage to bludgeoning, so the damaging effects do not retain cold damage, but the record still directly identifies a sorcerous caster with several cold spells and ice magic.

The Frostripper has an actual Primal innate spellcasting entry with multiple directly owned cold spells, including Howling Blizzard, Wall of Ice, and Frostbite, rather than merely a cold breath or environmental association. This is a creature using cold spellcasting and therefore a comparable caster for the authored intent.

Animal Pit is itself a weight-activated hidden pit trap: its description says a trap door covers a 10-by-20-foot pit, has a stealth DC, and the owned Pitfall action makes a triggering creature fall in. The named root is Animal Pit, but the owned action supplies the trap behavior for navigation.

Unstable Pit is an environmental pit hazard with a trap reaction that can make a creature slide into the pit, so it is useful for the pit portion of the intent. Its source explicitly says the formerly covered pit is now visible; only the unstable edge is not obvious, making it a qualified rather than a direct hidden-pit match.

The complex Riotous Mushrooms hazard’s routine directs an adjacent mushroom to use Poison Spores, which deals nonlethal poison damage to adjacent creatures. This is a useful environmental poison-spore exposure, but the source does not describe a gas cloud or say the spores disperse through the air, so it is a qualified match to poisonous gas.

The mask has Toxic Cloud linked to its Divine Innate Spells entry; the spell creates poisonous fog and deals poison damage to every breathing creature that starts its turn in the area. Its separate once-daily Evaporate Poison action can also turn an affliction into toxic vapor that exposes nearby creatures to brimstone fumes.

The Scarlet Triad Agent owns poisons and hollow blowgun darts for delivery, so it is substantively related to poison use. The source describes the Lethargy Poison and Purple Worm Venom as injury poisons activated by Interact; neither this equipment nor the agent’s listed mechanics expose people to poisonous gas.

Mother Venom’s spontaneous divine spell repertoire includes Stinking Cloud, a rank-3 poison-trait cloud of putrid mist that sickens creatures ending turns inside it. The linked spellcasting entry has rank-3 slots, so this is an owned gas-like poison effect available to the creature, not merely the unrelated venom in its melee poison item.

Gas Trap explicitly seals the room and pumps poison gas through four hidden vents. Its routine deals poison damage to breathing creatures each round and identifies blocking all vents as the way to disable it, a direct environmental poisonous-gas threat.

Befuddling Gas Trap is an environmental hazard whose description says seven concealed ceiling nozzles release poison gas when the room is closed with a creature inside. The gas causes stupefaction and mental damage rather than poison damage, but the authored intent does not require a specific damage type or saving-throw result.

Seoni directly owns a Lesser Antidote, the requested poison-protection consumable, with its one-use inventory quantity. The minor Elixir of Life is an additional poison-save aid, but the antidote alone makes this a direct equipment result.

Keznin carries two Moderate Antidotes, which protect against poisons, so this is a direct consumable match regardless of the requested dose tier. His expanded healer’s tools and Expert Herbalist action also support Treat Poison, but those are additional medical capabilities rather than the basis for the direct grade.

Yacob carries a Lesser Antidote, a direct poison-protection consumable, with one use recorded in the inventory. His healer’s tools support Treat Poison as a separate medical capability, but the owned antidote itself directly satisfies the equipment/consumable discovery intent.

Open the Wall of Ghosts is a ritual that opens the specifically named Wall of Ghosts and allows other creatures to pass through it. That is an actual passage through a barrier, but it applies to this singular supernatural wall and requires a day-long ritual at the specified lunar time, so it is a constrained route rather than a general wall-crossing answer.

Door to Beyond creates cracks that pull creatures toward a breach in reality, so it is substantively related to barriers and passage. Its description explicitly says the cracks are too thin for anything to fully slip through; it therefore cannot transport a creature through a wall or open a passable doorway.

The Annis Hag has Passwall in its Coven Spells casting entry, with a rank-5 innate slot and the spell linked to that entry. Passwall creates a tunnel through a wall that creatures can move through; this is a direct wall-crossing capability, with its source-record coven context stated rather than assumed away.

Darivan is explicitly a sorcerer, and his spontaneous Primal Spells entry includes Passwall linked at rank 5 with rank-5 spell slots. The spell creates a traversable tunnel through a wall, making this a direct match to passing through a solid barrier.

This familiar ability forms icy difficult terrain in a 5-foot burst, but it neither freezes creatures nor supplies an enclosed-room hazard.

Coerce is a minute-long Intimidation check that compels a creature to comply; it has no attack, reaction, or opportunity trigger corresponding to the old action.
Accidental Shot is a ranged Strike with a fortune benefit, so it is attack-related, but it is a once-daily action rather than a reaction to an opening.
A Moment Unending adds precision damage to a later Strike, making it substantively attack-related, but it has no reaction or triggering enemy action.

Reactive Strike is the source-verified renamed action: its reaction triggers when a nearby creature moves, manipulates, or makes a ranged attack, then makes a melee Strike and can disrupt a critical-hit manipulate action.
Foresight is a reaction to a target defending against danger, but it changes roll outcomes rather than making the counterattack that defined Attack of Opportunity.
Trip is an attack-trait maneuver against a creature’s Reflex DC; it is related to combat attacks but is not a reactive strike or old-name alias.
Escape removes grabbed, immobilized, or restrained conditions by checking against their source; its attack trait applies to the check, not to an opportunity attack.
Calculate Threats grants AC and Reflex bonuses against incoming attacks, a defense-related response but not the old action’s reactive Strike.
Overload Vision reacts when a creature attacks the user and can dazzle or blind it, so it is attack-triggered but does not make the requested counterattack.
Devise a Stratagem helps plan an attack roll against a chosen foe, but it is an action before the Strike rather than a reaction to an opening.
Exploit Vulnerability identifies a foe’s weakness and empowers later Strikes; that is combat-attack support, not an opportunity reaction or renamed action.
Strike is the basic attack used by Reactive Strike, but this generic action has no reaction, trigger, or old-name identity on its own.
Flyby Attack combines flight with a Strike, making it movement-and-attack related, but it is a two-action activity rather than a reaction to an enemy opening.
Amassed Assault damages enemies in a companion’s space, so it is a substantive offensive action but not a reactive single Strike or the renamed rule.
Threatening Approach is a Stride followed by Demoralize; its effects concern frightened, not attacks or reactions.
Opportunistic Accusation is a reaction that damages a demon after a specific vulnerability or save failure, but it does not counterattack a creature’s movement or manipulate opening.
Boarding Assault moves or swings and then makes a Strike; it is an attack after movement, not a reaction to an opponent’s movement.
Impromptu Investment swaps invested items over a minute and has no attack, reaction, or opportunity mechanic.
Opportune Riposte is a genuine reaction Strike, but its trigger is a foe critically failing a Strike against you, not the old action’s movement, manipulate, or ranged-attack triggers.
Feint sets up a later melee attack by making the target off-guard; it is attack-related but has no reaction or trigger matching Attack of Opportunity.
Sense Weakness is a reaction that makes a dueling opponent off-guard against an imminent melee Strike, but it modifies an attack instead of making an opportunity Strike.
Force Open can smash doors or walls with Athletics, but that object-breaking action is unrelated to the old reaction attack.
Inspired Stratagem is a reaction before an ally’s attack roll that grants fortune, so it is attack-roll related but does not counterattack or match the renamed action.

Implement’s Interruption is the closest qualified analogue: under Exploit Vulnerability and weapon-implement requirements it reacts to move, manipulate, or concentrate actions with a Strike and possible disruption, but it is a separate restricted feature rather than the renamed general action.
The snake is an electricity-themed creature with static attacks and a lightning strike that redirects energy absorbed from storms; those attacks do not make its body or identity a storm.
This is directly a living cloud: its authored description calls it a humanoid-shaped storm cloud, and its innate thunderbolt attack makes the storm embodiment concrete.
The metal sphere is a magnetic elemental; it reverses polarity when struck by electricity, but its active field manipulates metal rather than embodying or creating a storm.
This feat helps a character function in bad weather and grants no storm form or storm-producing power; weather familiarity is related but does not answer with an entity.
The hazard is a magical rune trap that releases void and sonic damage when someone approaches; thunder is only its roar, not a storm entity or storm manifestation.
The thunderbird is described as bringing storms on its wings and calling hurricanes; its controllable cyclone-and-driving-rain aura is an inherent, usable storm manifestation.
This air elemental is itself a swirling dust-devil-like whirlwind, with a high-winds aura and an action that creates violent wind; the identity and mechanics both embody storm-like air.
The rune is a constructed magical symbol, and its electricity attack is an energy-damage option; neither the identity nor the authored abilities make it a storm.
This autonomous rune can make an electrical blast, but its authored identity is a constructed written symbol and it has no storm embodiment or weather ability.
The source describes a connected grove of trees and plant-elemental behavior; the wind phrase occurs only in a camouflage effect ending, with no storm concept fit.
The storm lord is an air elemental explicitly identified with battles on the Plane of Air; its high-winds aura and lightning lash are built-in stormlike powers.

This is a useful constrained living-rain alternative: the swarm consists of storm-born creatures made when magical energy and rainfall transform the droplets into life, though the swarm is not itself a weather system.
This is a magically animated two-dimensional painting that moves on flat surfaces; its abilities concern surfaces and paint, not storms or weather.

The creature is an animate dream formed from dream fragments and fear. Thunderstrike is mentioned only as an example of a spell a designer might optionally choose, not as an actual storm power of this record.
Agyra is titled the Forever Storm and can generate a four-mile hurricane centered on herself; this is an explicit storm manifestation by the entity, alongside her lightning abilities.
This is another animated flat-surface painting; the blood-themed healing interaction and paint attacks do not supply any storm identity or capability.
The living waterfall is a humanoid column of churning water with aquatic vortex effects; it is a water elemental rather than a storm embodiment, though its flowing-water nature is related.
This background concerns surviving a maritime disaster and gaining weather sense and Weather Lore; it provides no entity or storm manifestation.

Sthira is an undead assemblage rather than a storm creature, but the actor has an associated primal innate-spell entry and a linked Storm of Vengeance spell, constrained here to hail each round; that is a useful storm-casting route.
The oil graffiti source describes a magically animated drawing restricted to flat surfaces; the oil/pigment theme has no storm connection.
This hazard creates a real lightning-and-tornado storm, but it is an environmental encounter hazard with a triggered event, not an entity embodying or manifesting as a storm.

Jesseri is not herself a storm, but her linked spontaneous primal repertoire includes Ice Storm and other weather effects such as wind and lightning; this is a useful spellcaster alternative, not an embodied storm.

Venomfist has an innate Wrathful Storm spell that creates a massive rain-and-gale cloud with selectable blizzard, hail, lightning, or tornado effects, and its own Toxic Downpour changes local weather; these are inherent storm manifestations.

Diskah is not a storm entity, but her linked prepared druid spells include Tempest Surge, which surrounds a foe with violent winds, clouds, and lightning; this is a usable but qualified storm-magic route.
The archer is a fey hunter whose hair moves in a gentle breeze; this is incidental atmosphere, while its listed cloudkill effect is poisonous fog, not storm embodiment.

This kineticist ability creates an actual miniature storm of dark thunderclouds and lightning, a useful storm-manifesting capability; the record is the attack action rather than an entity that embodies the storm.
This creature is a living mural whose relevant abilities are painting, blinding paint, and movement over flat surfaces; nothing makes it a storm.
Iogaka is explicitly a storm hag personifying a storm’s rage; its stormcalling ability can create hurricanes, thunderstorms, or tornadoes regardless of season.
Austral is an anemos whose true form is coalesced wind, and the source says cardinal anemoi direct world-spanning winds; this is an entity embodied as moving air.
The storm hag is expressly called the personification of a storm’s rage, and its stormcalling power actively creates severe weather; it directly answers the entity intent.
The hazard’s triggered effect is a wind-and-fire storm that throws debris and sharp rain, but the record is a nonliving hazard event rather than a storm entity.
This elemental embodies molten magma and volcanic eruptions, a fire/earth phenomenon rather than a storm or weather entity.
This living rune can cast Chain Lightning, but its source identity is a constructed glyph and its lightning is a spell attack rather than storm embodiment or weather power.
The giant’s prose says it embodies tempest fury and the calm of a hurricane’s eye; it also has at-will Control Weather, so its storm identity is backed by usable weather power.
This is a general archetypes journal. The cited [quotation omitted] language is a metaphor for a dual-weapon fighting style and the entry describes weapon attacks, not a living or manifesting storm.
The spell directly creates a cloud with selectable rain, wind, or fog and allows repeated lightning strikes, so it is a useful spell-level storm manifestation; it is not itself a living entity.
This is a magically animated chalk drawing that moves on flat surfaces; chalk and paint effects provide no storm connection.

Tormonshilds are living creatures literally formed from raindrops during artificially created storms, a constrained rain-born living alternative though the resulting frog-like individual is not itself a storm system.
This higher-level variant is still a nonliving hazard whose triggered storm of wind and fire attacks an area; it is related to storm manifestation but does not answer with an entity.
This boon records exposure to a tempest’s power and grants only minor cold and electricity resistance; it is a storm-associated benefit, not a storm entity or manifestation.
This is an earth-plane herd animal made of rock and metal; its description and abilities involve gliding through earth, not storm or weather.
This rule defines when an object is broken and what that state does, but it does not perform or provide a repair method. It is directly related context, not a useful repair answer.
Restore Ground destroys unattended objects while returning land to nature, so its object effect reverses the requested repair function rather than restoring damaged items.
Haphazard Repair lets an inventor quickly repair only their own innovation, and still requires adjacency and a repair kit; it is a useful but narrowly scoped repair option.

Sixth Pillar Student has Mending known in a spontaneous repertoire with 4 slot1 slots available; it restores item HP and can clear Broken once HP exceeds the threshold, while the rank-1 target is a nonmagical object of light Bulk or less and the spell cannot replace missing pieces or repair a destroyed object.

Vault Builder has Mending currently prepared in slot3; it restores item HP and can clear Broken once HP exceeds the threshold, while the rank-1 target is a nonmagical object of light Bulk or less and the spell cannot replace missing pieces or repair a destroyed object.
Desperate Repair prevents a shield that is about to hit 0 HP from being destroyed and leaves it at 1 HP, but it is a reactive rescue for that shield rather than repair of an already broken object.

Algerschmick has Mending an innate spell associated with the creature; it restores item HP and can clear Broken once HP exceeds the threshold, while the rank-1 target is a nonmagical object of light Bulk or less and the spell cannot replace missing pieces or repair a destroyed object.
Awaken Object grants an object awareness but does not repair it; it only says that an awakened object rendered insensate by Broken must be repaired by another means.

Grandmama has Mending an innate spell associated with the creature; it restores item HP and can clear Broken once HP exceeds the threshold, while the rank-1 target is a nonmagical object of light Bulk or less and the spell cannot replace missing pieces or repair a destroyed object.
The Repair action is the direct method: with a repair kit and 10 minutes, a Crafting check restores item HP; it cannot repair a destroyed item.

Fumbus has a carried repair kit in his backpack, Crafting rank 2, and a worn Crafter’s Eyepiece that improves Repair restoration; he can perform ordinary Repair checks, subject to their DC and the destroyed-item limit.

Remake can restore an object even after destruction and returns it in perfect condition, but it needs a remnant and an accurate mental image and excludes oversized, artifact-level, or still-existing targets.
Rite of Repatriation repairs HP damage only for a culturally important object since its last possession by rightful owners; it cannot replace missing pieces or repair a destroyed object.

Flicker is an eligible spell, but its source describes plane-phasing resistance and random 10-foot teleportation, not the named Fly spell or flight capability. The spell-type filter is satisfied while the source itself is not a useful Fly match.
Wall Run lets the user Stride along vertical surfaces and then fall if the movement ends off the ground; it traverses a wall surface rather than passing through a solid wall.

Il'setsya has Passwall in its Arcane Spontaneous Spells entry. That spell creates a tunnel through a wall, directly enabling passage; it is limited to 10 feet of wall depth by default and fails if the wall contains even a small layer of metal.

Ilgreth’s Prepared Arcane Spells include Fly, and its spell ID is actually prepared in a fourth-rank slot, so the actor can cast the spell. This is a useful owner record for finding Fly, while remaining a creature copy rather than the root spell or a separate Fly action record.

The Forest Dragon’s root lore explicitly says forest dragons protect nature from plunder and reclaim ruins for wilderness, and identifies them literally with their forests. This directly fits an entity that guards a forest.
This rule record is specifically Toxic Breath and describes a cloud of toxic gas that damages all creatures in a cone, directly matching a poisonous-gas danger.

Door to Beyond creates cracks and pulls creatures toward them, but its description expressly says nothing can pass fully through the cracks. It is related to a door/barrier and spatial movement but does not provide a way through a wall.

Frostripper is a kokogiak rather than a sorcerer, but its Primal Innate Spells include Howling Blizzard, Wall of Ice, and Frostbite with explicit cold damage and effects. The actual source therefore supports a comparable caster using several cold spells, not just cold breath.

Nightwood guardians patrol the nightwoods to preserve their perpetual shadow and drive out intruders. Although this is a specialized forest-like region on the Plane of Wood, its root lore directly assigns the creature a protective guardian role.
The full creature entry describes living two-dimensional art that moves across surfaces and uses chalk or paint to attack, with no storm identity or storm powers; it is unrelated to a living storm.

Dragonstorm includes a Freezing Wind effect that deals cold damage, but the source is a localized multi-effect storm hazard rather than an enclosed room hazard, and its cold effect slows on a critical failure rather than freezing occupants.

Clownish Curse applies misfortune to its target: the target rolls twice and uses the worse result on specified checks, the reverse of retrying or replacing an unlucky result.

Show the Path lets its target roll a d20 at the start of each turn and substitute that result for any check before the next turn, directly replacing a later check result; the timing and repeated-use bonus are stated.
Cat’s Luck is a once-per-day reaction triggered by a failed Reflex save and lets the user reroll that save using the better result.
Turn Away Misfortune can cancel a misfortune effect on a roll so the user rolls normally, but it does not reroll or replace a result already obtained.
Lem’s owned Halfling Luck ancestry feat triggers when he fails a skill check or saving throw and lets him reroll that check once per day; he must use the new result even if worse.
Pharaoh’s Ward is a genuine magical curse hazard, but its stated effects are a Fortitude penalty and halved healing; it does not age affected creatures.

The Pale Sovereign’s lore describes a curse that drains a royal victim’s vitality into a wasting disease and eventual death, but it does not say the victim unnaturally ages; the creature’s undead identity is a result of that curse.

The Archetypes journal’s age references concern disguise age or historical eras and do not describe a curse or an effect that unnaturally ages a victim.
